A Call to Conscience: The True Cost of Corruption in Flood Control

Every time floodwaters rise in Metro Manila, it’s not just rain that drowns our streets—it’s the weight of corruption that submerges our hopes, our health, and our future.

Senator Panfilo Lacson’s revelation that ₱1 trillion—half of the ₱2 trillion allocated to flood control since 2011—may have been lost to corruption is not just a statistic 

It is a betrayal. A betrayal of every child who misses school because classrooms are flooded. A betrayal of every worker stranded, every patient unable to reach a hospital, every family forced to wade through disease-ridden waters.

Flooding is no longer just a seasonal inconvenience. It is a systemic failure—one that cripples our economy, disrupts education, endangers public health, and robs Filipinos of dignity and opportunity. 

The Department of Public Works and Highways was entrusted with safeguarding our communities. Instead, we are left with clogged drains, broken promises, and billions unaccounted for. 

This is not just about infrastructure. It is about integrity.

We must demand a full audit of flood control spending. 

We must hold accountable those who treat public funds as personal gain. 

And we must insist on a governance that values transparency, resilience, and moral leadership.

Let this be our turning point. Let the floods awaken not just outrage—but action.

Because when corruption floods our institutions, it is the people who drown.

Dr. Tony Leachon 

Cc 
@iampinglacson
